title: What is science?
competency: Define science and tell indigenous science from conventional science, with Ethiopian examples.

keywords.def: A systematic way of learning about the natural and physical world and human society, based on observation and evidence.
Knowledge that local people build from long experience of their environment, based on social, physical and spiritual understanding.
Knowledge based on laws found by using the scientific method on events in the world. Often called Western science.
An orderly way to find out: observe, test, and check the evidence.
A plant that people use for treating and curing diseases, such as the kosso tree.

en.text: The word science comes from the Latin word scientia, meaning knowledge. But science is more than having knowledge. It is an orderly way of learning about nature and human society. It is based on observation and evidence.

am.text: ሳይንስ የሚለው ቃል ‹ሳይንሺያ› ከሚለው የላቲን ቃል የመጣ ሲሆን ትርጉሙ እውቀት ነው። ሳይንስ ግን እውቀት ከመያዝ በላይ ነው። ስለ ተፈጥሮና ስለ ሰው ማህበረሰብ በሥርዓት የምንማርበት መንገድ ነው። በምልከታና በማስረጃ ላይ የተመሠረተ ነው።

screens.title: Will it rain?
screens.text: Your grandmother says dark clouds over Entoto mean rain. You want to know if she is right.
opts: Watch the clouds and record the rain for many days
screens.after:
A scientist does not just believe or ignore an idea.
She watches the clouds and writes down the rain for many days.
Then the evidence shows if grandmother is right.
This orderly way of finding out is science. Read on.
screens.best: Watch the clouds and record the rain for many days

screens.title: Science in Grade 7
paras: In lower grades you learnt science in general, like environmental science.
In Grades 7 and 8 you study General Science. It is about your daily life.

screens.title: Where the word comes from
paras: Science comes from the Latin word scientia. Scientia means "knowledge".
But science is more than knowledge. It is a systematic (orderly) way of gaining it.

screens.title: What science studies
paras: Science studies the physical and natural world and human society.
It shows what things are like. It is based on observation and evidence.

screens.title: What science looks at
screens.ask: Tap each card to see what science studies and how.
items: Science starts by watching carefully, like counting seeds that sprout.
Science writes down what it sees. The records are evidence.
Science studies living things, matter and energy.
Science also studies people and how they live together.

screens.title: Science is a way of knowing
defs: A systematic method of gaining knowledge about the physical and natural world and human society. It is based on observation and evidence.

screens.title: More than knowledge
screens.text: What makes science more than just "having knowledge"?
opts: It is only what happens in laboratories
It is guessing until you are right
It is an orderly way of getting knowledge, based on observation and evidence
screens.ans: It is an orderly way of getting knowledge, based on observation and evidence
screens.why:
Science is not only a store of facts.
It is a systematic (orderly) way of gaining knowledge.
It is based on observation and evidence.
So the answer is: an orderly way of getting knowledge, based on observation and evidence.
"Only memorising facts" is tempting, but that misses the method.
screens.clue: Look for the words "systematic method" and "evidence" in the text.

screens.title: The Latin root
screens.ask: Word origin: the word science comes from the Latin word ___, which means knowledge.
screens.why:
The English word science comes from Latin.
The Latin word is scientia.
Scientia means "knowledge".
So the answer is scientia.
screens.clue: It is a Latin word that starts like "science".

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: What science is based on: science is based on observation and evidence.
screens.why:
The book says science shows what things are like.
It says science is based on observation and evidence.
The statement repeats this exactly.
So it is true.

screens.title: Teff seeds
screens.text: Almaz plants teff seeds in wet soil and in dry soil. Each day she counts the seeds that sprout and writes the numbers.
opts: No, because she is not in a laboratory
Yes, because she gathers evidence by observing in an orderly way
No, because she already knows the answer
Yes, because she memorised a fact
screens.ans: Yes, because she gathers evidence by observing in an orderly way
screens.why:
Step 1: what does Almaz do? She observes seeds every day.
Step 2: she writes the numbers down. That is evidence.
Step 3: science is an orderly way of learning from observation and evidence.
Step 4: science does not need a laboratory.
So yes, she is doing science.
screens.clue: Does science need a laboratory, or does it need orderly observation?
screens.worked:
Step 1: Almaz plants seeds in wet soil and in dry soil.
Step 2: each day she counts the sprouting seeds and records the numbers.
Step 3: recorded counts are evidence, gathered in an orderly way.
Step 4: science is a systematic way of learning based on observation and evidence.
So yes, she is doing science, even outside a laboratory.

en.text: Science can be indigenous or conventional. Indigenous science is knowledge local people build from long experience of their environment. Conventional science relies on laws found with the scientific method. It is often called Western science.

am.text: ሳይንስ ሀገር በቀል ወይም ዘመናዊ ሊሆን ይችላል። ሀገር በቀል ሳይንስ የአካባቢው ሰዎች ከአካባቢያቸው ጋር ባላቸው ረጅም ልምድ የሚገነቡት እውቀት ነው። ዘመናዊ ሳይንስ በሳይንሳዊ ዘዴ በተገኙ ሕጎች ላይ ይመሠረታል። ብዙ ጊዜ የምዕራባውያን ሳይንስ ይባላል።

screens.title: Where did we learn it?
screens.text: Before you read, sort these. Where does each piece of knowledge come from?
bins: Learnt from tests in a laboratory
items: Preserving meat with salt and smoke drying
Families have done this for a long time.
Learnt from tests in a laboratory
A microscope is a laboratory tool.
Local people learnt this plant's use over many years.
Testing a new medicine on bacteria in a dish
Learnt from tests in a laboratory
This is a planned laboratory test.
Keeping grain safe with methods from grandparents
The method passed from elders to children.

screens.title: Two kinds of science
paras: Indigenous science is knowledge local people build from experience of their environment. It rests on social, physical and spiritual understanding.
Conventional science relies on laws found with the scientific method. It is commonly called Western science.
screens.note: Science grew from many cultures. "Western" is only a common label.

screens.title: Two kinds of science
items: Built by local people from long experience, like kosso as medicine.
Laws found with the scientific method, often in a laboratory.

screens.title: Name the two kinds
defs: Knowledge local people build from long experience of their natural environment.
Knowledge based on laws found with the scientific method. Commonly called Western science.
An orderly way to find out: observe, test, and check the evidence.

screens.title: Keeping grain safe
screens.text: A family has kept grain safe for generations. They use local methods learnt from their elders.
screens.why:
Step 1: where did the family learn the method? From their elders.
Step 2: it comes from long experience of their own environment.
Step 3: knowledge built that way by local people is indigenous science.
So the answer is indigenous science.
Conventional science would need laws found with the scientific method.
screens.clue: Which kind of science comes from local people and their surroundings?
screens.ask: Which kind of science is this mainly an example of?

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: What conventional science relies on: conventional science relies on laws found by applying the scientific method.
screens.why:
The book defines conventional science.
It relies on laws found with the scientific method.
The statement says the same thing.
So it is true.

screens.title: Another name
screens.ask: Another name: conventional science is commonly called ___ science.
screens.why:
The book gives conventional science a common name.
It is commonly called Western science.
So the answer is Western.
Remember: "Western" is only a label. Science grew from many cultures.
screens.clue: Think of a direction on the compass.

screens.title: Frost in the highlands
screens.text: A farmer near Debre Birhan looks at the night sky. He says frost will come. His father taught him this sign.
screens.why:
Step 1: who taught the farmer the frost sign? His father.
Step 2: so the knowledge was passed down from local experience.
Step 3: he did not use a law found in a laboratory.
Step 4: local knowledge from experience is indigenous science.
So the answer is indigenous science.
screens.clue: Did he learn it from a laboratory law, or from his elders?
screens.ask: Which kind of knowledge is he using?
screens.worked:
Step 1: the farmer reads a sign in the night sky.
Step 2: his father taught him this sign. It comes from long local experience.
Step 3: he did not test it with the scientific method in a laboratory.
So he is using indigenous science.

en.text: We learn indigenous knowledge for two reasons. It makes us aware of our own culture and identity. It also lets us join it with Western science. In Ethiopia, people make medicine from plants and preserve meat with salt and smoke drying.

am.text: ሀገር በቀል እውቀትን የምንማረው በሁለት ምክንያቶች ነው። ስለ ራሳችን ባህልና ማንነት እንድናውቅ ያደርገናል። ከምዕራባውያን ሳይንስ ጋር እንድናጣምረውም ያስችለናል። በኢትዮጵያ ሰዎች ከተክሎች መድኃኒት ይሠራሉ፤ ሥጋንም በጨውና በጭስ በማድረቅ ያቆያሉ።

screens.title: Before fridges
screens.text: Long ago, villages in Ethiopia had no fridges. Meat goes bad in a few days.
screens.ask: How do you think families kept meat for a long time?
opts: Leaving it wet in the sun
screens.after:
Salt pulls water out of meat. Smoke drying dries it more.
Dry meat goes bad much more slowly.
Families learnt this from long experience, not from a laboratory.
This is indigenous knowledge. Read on.

screens.title: Why learn indigenous knowledge?
paras: First, it makes us more aware of our own culture and identity.
Second, it lets us join indigenous knowledge with Western science.

screens.title: Indigenous knowledge in Ethiopia
paras: Ethiopia has a wide variety of indigenous knowledge. People long used it to solve practical problems.
One example is medicine from plants against disease and infection. Another is preserving meat with salt and smoke drying.

screens.caption: Medicinal plants treat and cure diseases.

screens.title: Medicinal plants
paras: People use these plants for treating and curing diseases.
screens.note: Never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker tells you how.

screens.title: Three medicinal plants
screens.ask: Tap each plant to see its scientific name.
items: Scientific name: Hagenia abyssinica. "Abyssinica" comes from Abyssinia, an old name for Ethiopia.
Scientific name: Eucalyptus globulus. It is the eucalyptus tree.

screens.title: Plants that heal
defs: A plant that people use for treating and curing diseases. Kosso, bahrzaf and damakese are examples.

screens.title: Spot the example
screens.text: Which of these is an example of Ethiopian indigenous knowledge?
opts: Heating liquid with a Bunsen burner
Using kosso, bahrzaf or damakese plants to treat illness
Using a microscope to see cells
screens.ans: Using kosso, bahrzaf or damakese plants to treat illness
screens.why:
Step 1: indigenous knowledge comes from local people and long experience.
Step 2: kosso, bahrzaf and damakese are local medicinal plants.
Step 3: people have used them for a long time to treat illness.
So the answer is using these plants to treat illness.
Bunsen burners, lab reports and microscopes belong to conventional science.
screens.clue: Think about knowledge that comes from local plants and people.

screens.title: Local and scientific names
screens.text: Medicinal plants: match each local name to its scientific name.
screens.why:
The book's table of medicinal plants gives each pair.
Kosso tree → Hagenia abyssinica.
Bahrzaf (the eucalyptus tree) → Eucalyptus globulus.
Damakese → Ocimum lamiifolium.
Tip: "abyssinica" comes from Abyssinia, an old name for Ethiopia.
screens.clue: Look back at the table. Bahrzaf is the eucalyptus tree.

screens.title: Two reasons
screens.ask: Why learn indigenous knowledge? It makes us more aware of our own culture and ___.
screens.why:
The book gives two reasons to learn indigenous knowledge.
First: it makes us more aware of our own culture and identity.
Second: it lets us join it with Western science.
So the answer is identity.
screens.clue: Read the first reason in "Why learn indigenous knowledge?".

screens.title: A sick cousin
screens.text: Medicine safety: Hanna's cousin feels sick. Hanna should boil damakese leaves and give them to him without asking anyone.
screens.why:
Step 1: damakese is a medicinal plant in the book.
Step 2: but the book does not say how to use it, or how much.
Step 3: the wrong plant or amount can make someone sicker.
Step 4: the rule is: ask a health worker or a knowledgeable adult first.
So the statement is false.
screens.clue: Read the safety note under the plant table.
screens.worked:
Step 1: the book lists damakese as a medicinal plant.
Step 2: it does not say which illness it treats, or how to use it.
Step 3: the safety note says: never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker tells you how.
So the statement is false.

opts: A systematic way of learning about the world, based on observation and evidence
A list of facts to memorise
test.ans: A systematic way of learning about the world, based on observation and evidence
test.why:
Science is a systematic (orderly) way of learning.
It studies the natural and physical world and human society.
It is based on observation and evidence.
So the first statement is best.
"A list of facts" misses the method; "beliefs never tested" is the opposite of science.

test.text: Indigenous knowledge: preserving meat with salt and smoke drying is an example of indigenous knowledge.
test.why:
Indigenous knowledge is built by local people from long experience.
Ethiopian families have preserved meat with salt and smoke drying for a long time.
They learnt it from elders, not from a laboratory.
So the statement is true.

test.ask: Scientific names: the scientific name of the kosso tree is Hagenia ___.
test.why:
The book's table lists the kosso tree.
Its scientific name is Hagenia abyssinica.
So the missing word is abyssinica.

notes.text: The printed book has no heading "1.1.1". It jumps from "1.1" to the introduction. The heading is added so the numbering matches 1.1.2, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4.
Modern science has grown from the work of people in many cultures, so "Western" is only a common label, not the whole story.
The book does not say which diseases each plant treats. Never use a plant as medicine unless a health worker or a knowledgeable adult tells you how.
Hooks and the word problems marked "added" are not in the book; they use Ethiopian settings to introduce the book's ideas.
Visual-first pass: read blocks shortened (no facts dropped) and drawings from app/pictures.js added.
Rule 14/15 upgrade (2026-10-24): step-by-step why on every graded item, best on guess hooks, and added interactive blocks (marked added).
